title: Investigating Intersectional Bias in Large Language Models using Confidence Disparities in Coreference Resolution
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the 'Coreference Confidence Disparity' for various intersectional identities. For religion, it specifically measured whether models were more or less confident in resolving coreferences for prompts that included Christian, Muslim, or Jewish demographic markers, particularly when intersected with gender.
findings: The study found that while models showed confidence disparities across most demographic attributes, the disparities were smallest along the axes of age, nationality, and religion. This indicates that religious identity, compared to attributes like body type or socio-economic status, induced less of a drop in model confidence for the coreference resolution task.
